A telephone , commonly shortened to phone , is a telecommunications device that enables two or more users to conduct a conversation when they are too far apart to be easily heard directly. A telephone converts sound , typically and most efficiently the human voice , into electronic signals that are transmitted via cables and other communication channels to another telephone which reproduces the sound to the receiving user. The term is derived from Ancient Greek : τῆλε , romanized : tēle , lit. ' far ' and φωνή ( phōnē , voice ), together meaning distant voice . [ 1 ]
